question.text: Inventory on the balance sheet is shown at:

answer.text: Cost price or market value, whichever is lower
Original purchase price only regardless of current value

explanation.text: The Logic: Per the workbook (page 150), inventory is shown on the balance sheet at cost price or market value, whichever is lower. This conservative approach avoids overstating assets. The Trap: Inventory is not always carried at cost (it can be written down when market value is lower) and is not shown at replacement cost or at inflated market values. Note: When analysing a company, persistently high finished-goods or raw-material inventory levels (page 174) can be a red flag worth investigating further.
